title.zh: 入射中性边界通量归一化

summary: Scale a caller-owned H or H2 boundary shape distribution on the positive axial-velocity half space to a requested incoming neutral particle flux, returning the scaled boundary distribution, the normalization scale, and the pre-scale flux integral.

capability: Scale a caller-owned H or H2 boundary shape distribution on the positive axial-velocity half space to a requested incoming neutral particle flux, returning the scaled boundary distribution, the normalization scale, and the pre-scale flux integral.
operation: normalize an incoming neutral boundary flux
boundary shape plus axes, volume, thermal speed and target flux -> scaled boundary, scale, incoming flux
discovery.geometry: one radial dimension times the axial velocity axis
discovery.boundary: finite nonnegative (nvr,nvx) shape and volume, finite positive thermal speed and finite target; positive original incoming flux; all public values finite, with separate 64*eps relative and zero absolute representation budgets for the original flux, normalization factor and actual returned-cell flux, eps=2^-52

identity.relation: the positive-half flux normalization: incoming_flux = Vth * sum(volume * shape * vx) over vx > 0; scale = abs(target_flux) / incoming_flux
identity.direction: boundary shape plus axes, volume, thermal speed and target flux -> scaled boundary, scale, incoming flux
identity.definition: Only positive-vx cells enter the exact original integral Phi0=Vth*sum(volume*shape*vx). The continuous factor is s=abs(target)/Phi0; equal-magnitude signed targets have the same normalization, and a zero target gives zero scale and boundary. Three separate relative errors must each be at most 64*eps, with zero absolute allowance, eps=2^-52: returned incoming_flux against Phi0, returned scale against s, and the exact flux carried by returned cells against abs(target). A paired positive-sum interval or exact binary-rational integration certifies the errors; the original-flux interval is also propagated into the scale ratio. If necessary use exact Phi0 and s, then round each shape*s cell once. Rounded scale multiplication need not reproduce the boundary bitwise, but the public scalar itself must meet the relative budget. If even the nearest float64 scalar or this rounded normalized shape cannot meet its budget, raise ValueError; do not redistribute cells or change shape to force the integral. The nonpositive-vx half is exactly zero.
identity.geometry: one radial dimension times the axial velocity axis
identity.coordinates: shape and volume in the source's normalized units, vx in normalized axial speed, thermal speed m/s, target flux m^-2 s^-1
identity.boundary: finite nonnegative (nvr,nvx) shape and volume, finite positive thermal speed and finite target; positive original incoming flux; all public values finite, with separate 64*eps relative and zero absolute representation budgets for the original flux, normalization factor and actual returned-cell flux, eps=2^-52
assumptions: The caller owns the boundary shape and the quadrature; this asset normalizes, it does not construct a distribution.
The sign convention of the requested flux is the caller's (the scale uses abs); this function does not preserve target sign in its returned distribution.

inputs.name: boundary_shape
inputs.constraints: Finite nonnegative real numeric values; axial velocity on the second axis. Boolean, string and complex coercions are rejected.

inputs.name: vx
inputs.constraints: Finite real numeric one-dimensional axis; must contain at least one positive node. Boolean, string and complex coercions are rejected.

inputs.name: cylindrical_volume
inputs.constraints: Finite nonnegative real numeric values, same shape as the boundary shape. Boolean, string and complex coercions are rejected.

inputs.name: thermal_speed_m_s
inputs.constraints: Finite strictly positive real numeric scalar; booleans, strings, complex values and nonscalars are rejected.

inputs.name: target_flux_m2_s
inputs.constraints: Finite real numeric scalar of any sign, including zero; booleans, strings, complex values and nonscalars are rejected.

outputs.name: incoming_boundary
outputs.constraints: Finite; zero on the nonpositive-vx half. The positive-half flux of the actual returned cells matches abs(target_flux_m2_s) within 64*eps relative error and zero absolute error, where eps=2^-52. Tiny individual cells may round to zero.

outputs.name: scale
outputs.description: The continuous normalization factor represented as a float64 scalar.
outputs.constraints: Finite and nonnegative; positive for a nonzero target and zero for a zero target. Relative error against abs(target)/the exact original flux is at most 64*eps, with zero absolute error. Multiplying boundary_shape by this rounded scalar need not reproduce the returned cells bitwise.

outputs.name: incoming_flux
outputs.constraints: Finite and positive; relative error against the exact original positive-half flux is at most 64*eps, with zero absolute error.

preconditions: Finite nonnegative shape and volume, finite positive thermal speed, a positive-vx half with positive flux.
supported: Boundary sources for H and H2 inflow conditions on a shared normalized mesh.
excluded: Shapes with nonpositive flux on the positive half; meshes without a positive-vx node; non-finite scalars.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for boolean, string, complex or nonscalar values outside the declared shapes, non-finite or negative shape/volume, non-finite vx or scalars, nonpositive thermal speed, no positive vx node, or nonpositive positive-half flux.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError if the initial flux or scale cannot be represented within 64*eps relative error and zero absolute error, a normalized cell cannot be finite, or the actual returned-cell flux misses that same relative budget against abs(target). No physical fallback or altered shape is selected.
failure_semantics.partial_results: Never returned; a rejected call produces no result.

example.description: Normalize one boundary shape to a requested flux and confirm the positive-half semantics and rejections.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.neutrals import normalize_incoming_neutral_boundary
shape = np.ones((2, 3))
volume = np.ones((2, 3))
vx = np.array([-1.0, 0.5, 1.0])
result, scale, initial = normalize_incoming_neutral_boundary(shape, vx, volume, 2.0, -12.0)
assert initial == 6.0 and scale == 2.0
assert np.all(result[:, 0] == 0.0)
try:
    normalize_incoming_neutral_boundary(shape, np.array([-1.0, -0.5, 0.0]), volume, 2.0, 12.0)
except ValueError as error:
    assert 'positive incoming half' in str(error)
else:
    raise AssertionError('a mesh without a positive-vx node must be rejected')
example.expected: Observed PASS: The positive half scaled to the requested flux (sign-independent scale), the negative half exactly zero; a mesh without an incoming half is rejected.

scope: On the tested finite carriers, the returned positive-half flux integral after scaling equals the absolute requested target.
That the negative half is exactly zero and the scale matches the abs(target)/flux form.
The fail-closed contracts, including real finite inputs, nonnegative volume and finite derived outputs; zero target remains a valid zero boundary.

A nonzero target with every flux-carrying returned cell rounded to zero is rejected, even if a zero-volume cell stays positive. Controls retain a representable subnormal distribution and allow unrelated small cells to round to zero; an exact binary-rational flux oracle avoids a false rejection from reintegration underflow.

The frozen shape=[1,2], speed=1024, target=2^-1063 witness is rejected because the nearest representable public scale itself has 50% relative error. An exact scale=MIN control retains its subnormal boundary and exact flux. Signed targets, reversed cells, three NumPy error policies, pre-scale flux with +1/3 representation error even at zero target, unrepresentable quantized targets, compensated original integrals and nonuniform multicell inputs retain the frozen 1e-13/zero-absolute test budget.

Independent evidence (tests/neutrals/test_boundary_and_shape_normalization_evidence.py): the returned-cell flux is recomputed exactly in rational arithmetic and required to meet the contract's own 64/2**52 relative budget with zero absolute allowance, the initial flux and scale are separately certified against their exact values, a negative target gives the same scale and boundary, a zero target is the exact zero branch, and a volume below 2**-128 exercises the exact-arithmetic path.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Direct tests compare independent exact original-input and returned-cell integrals and the exact continuous normalization ratio. The implementation certifies three separate 64*eps relative, zero absolute budgets for the original flux, scale and returned-cell flux, strictly inside the frozen 1e-13 budget. This is numerical normalization evidence, not caller-owned distribution physics, complete transport or experimental validation. C1 evidence adds: exact rational certification of the returned cells and of the two public scalars, the target-sign symmetry, the zero branch and the exact-arithmetic fallback; it does not establish that the requested target flux is physically appropriate.
known_limitations: The historical function accepts some coercible non-real inputs and does not fully enforce finite quadrature or derived outputs; SciRel rejects them. A zero target is valid and produces zero scale, contrary to the intake document's positive-scale wording.

The public initial flux and normalization scale each require finite float64 representations within the relative budget, even if a boundary alone could carry the target. Each returned cell must be finite; the actual returned-cell flux must meet the same budget. Rounded scale multiplication need not reproduce single-rounded cells bitwise, but large scalar relative error is never accepted. Failure does not trigger another shape or redistribution of cells.

The budget is relative with zero absolute allowance, so a target at the very bottom of the float range is rejected rather than met; the normalization also cannot recover shape information that underflowed in the caller's cells.

basis.statement: Exact rational certification of the returned cells and of the two public scalars, the target-sign symmetry, the zero branch and the exact-arithmetic fallback decide the normalization. That the request is physically consistent is not established.
